I’ll find where the command parses trace IDs, trim whitespace around each ID, and add a regression test. I’ll use the repository’s Python style guidance and run only the relevant tests.
The regression test already staged in the workspace reproduces the bug. I’ll extend it to cover whitespace before and after IDs, then apply the fix. Pytest’s resource summary hit a sandbox permission error after the test; I’ll disable that summary for the next run.
Updated trace deletion to strip leading and trailing whitespace from each comma-separated ID, so `"a, b"` works like `"a,b"`.

Extended the existing regression test to cover spaces and tabs and verify the normalized IDs reach the deletion client.

Validation: all 12 tests in `tests/cli/test_traces.py` passed. Used `--no-summary` to avoid a sandbox-restricted resource-reporting hook. No dependencies installed.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("trace_ids", ["tr-1,tr-2", "tr-1, tr-2", " \ttr-1 \t, \ttr-2 \t"])
+def test_delete_command_strips_spaces_in_trace_ids(runner, trace_ids):
+    with mock.patch("mlflow.cli.traces.TracingClient.delete_traces", return_value=2) as mock_delete:
+        result = runner.invoke(
+            commands,
+            ["delete", "--experiment-id", "1", "--trace-ids", trace_ids],
+        )
+
+    assert result.exit_code == 0
+    assert "Deleted 2 trace(s)" in result.output
+    mock_delete.assert_called_once_with(
+        experiment_id="1",
+        trace_ids=["tr-1", "tr-2"],
+        max_timestamp_millis=None,
+        max_traces=None,
+    )
+
